6. Eventually, after filing of the said written statements the case was taken up by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhola for recording evidence of the parties. The 1st party and the contesting other parties of the case including the predecessors of the present petitioners had thereafter adduced their respective witnesses in support of their claim by placing their oral and documentary evidences in the case. 

 9. Feeling aggrieved by the said judgment and order of the learned Magistrate dated 23-6-2011, the 2nd, 4th and 5th parties i.e. the present petitioners herein unsuccessfully preferred Criminal Revision No. 96 of 2011 under section 439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Bhola who after hearing the parties concerned and also perusing the materials on record as well as the impugned judgment and order dated 23-6-2011 vide his judgment and order dated 17-1-2013 disallowing the Criminal Revision No. 96 of 2011 upheld the aforesaid judgment and order as was passed by the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhola in MR Case No. 129 of 1973. 

 12. While Ms Zubaida Gulshanara, learned Advocate appearing for the 2nd, 4th & 5th party petitioners, at the very outset, submitted that the learned Magistrate concerned as well as the revisional Court upon non-consideration of the material evidences on record as adduced by the 2nd, 4th and 5th party petitioners but in a surmise and conjecture manner passed the impugned judgment and orders relying only the 1st party's evidences. She also contended that both the Courts below in passing the impugned judgment and orders have cited the evidences as of the 1st and 3rd party's only but nothing of the other parties. She further submitted that though the 1st and 3rd party were failed to show their title and possession over the disputed land with very specification but the learned Judge of the. Courts below without taking the same in their consideration, rather non-applying their judicial mind passed the impugned judgment and orders which requires of this Hon'ble Court's interference. She further added to her submissions that the 2nd party was though died during pendency of the proceeding but the learned Magistrate concerned was failed to add his heirs in the proceeding which has caused gross mistake in the impugned judgments. 

 14. The learned Advocate for the petitioner lastly placed her submission to the extent that even though the 1st and 3rd party were failed to prove how and where they have possessed on the disputed land and on what basis of the documents they claimed their title over the property in question; as because the recent record-of-rights have not been prepared in their names. But the learned Judge of the Courts below were failed to take those material facts into their consideration in passing the impugned judgment and orders. Learned Advocate in support of her above submissions though referred to us a judgment passed by a Division Bench of this Court, in the case of Mozaffar Ahmed vs State, reported in 49 DLR 485; but that decision appears to us do not support the petitioners' case; because of that in the said judgment a Division Bench of this Court held that— 

 15. In contrary to the submissions as advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, Mr Shihab Uddin Mahmood, learned Advocate for the 1st party opposite party Nos. 1-9 submitted that the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bhola as well as the learned Sessions Judge, Bhola upon proper appreciation of law as well as after perusal of the material evidences on record rightly passed the impugned judgment and orders upon making concurrent findings thereto of their own; which deserves no interference. He also submitted that since this Court is now seating in extraordinary inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. as per the settled principle of our apex Court's judgment, this Court cannot re-assess the evidences of the trial Court. He further submitted that since the order of the learned Magistrate passed under section 145 CrPC is the final order; as such, this Hon'ble Court under section 561A only can see whether there has been any coram non-judice or there has been barred by any law or has there any abuse of the process of the Court, but nothing else. In support of is such submissions learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos. 1-9 referred to us the judgment passed in the case of Azmal Mia vs Md Alaluddin Chowdhury, reported in 1 MLR (AD) (1996) 410. He also referred to us the case of Shamsuddin alias Shamsuddoha vs Moulvi Amzad Ali, reported in 9 MLR (AD) (2004) 32 = 56 DLR (AD) 59. He then referred another decision of this sub-continent, the case of Waved Chand vs Dr Revel Chand & Faquir Chand, reported in AIR (1941) (Lahore) 227: and submitted to that extent that in all the above cases their Lordships of the apex Court reiterated their same views as of the limited scope of the High Court Division in examining the Magistrate's order passed under section 145 of CrPC which has been ultimately challenged before the Sessions Judge in revision under section 439A of CrPC. 

 17. In order to appreciate the above submissions of the respective parties, we have gone through the record and perused the impugned judgment and orders. We have also considered the submissions as placed before us by the learned Advocates for the contending parties. It appears from the record that the petitioners in filing the present petition under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure annexed therewith only the impugned judgment and orders of the Courts below and the petition of complaint as was filed by the 1st party in MR Case No. 129 of 1973, but nothing else. From the Rule issuance order it reveals that the lower Court's record has not been called for. In such prevailing situation it is difficult to us to examine the petitioners' claim as advanced in their submissions before us. However, seating in an extraordinary inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure this Court has a limited scope to travel in its jurisdiction while examining the revisional Court's judgment in a case where no appeal lies. Moreover, this Court under the said jurisdiction cannot re-assess the evidences placed before a competent Court of law as per the enunciation made by our apex Court. In the case of Abdul Quader Chowdhury vs State, reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38, our apex Court has determined certain criterion about to invoke jurisdiction under section 561A. As per the said decision this Court can only to see whether there has been any coram non-judice in passing the impugned judgment and order, or there has been barred by any law and/or to see for ends of justice whether there has been any abuse of the process of the Court. 

 21. However, upon perusal of both the judgments of the Courts below we find that there is nothing any abuse of the process of the Court and nothing has been raised to that extent on behalf of the petitioners, even of any coram non-judice. Further that no legal bar appears to be present in running the instant, proceeding. As such, with regard to address the petitioner's submissions we are of the opinion that seating in an extraordinary inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal. Procedure, we are very much undone to re-assess the evidences as adduced and has been considered by the competent Court of law i.e. the learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate; who is the right authority under the law to pass such order under section 145, CrPC upon evaluating the evidences placed before him. Later in revision under section 439A of CrPC the learned Sessions Judge, Bhola upon addressing to the points raised on behalf of petitioners whether the 2nd party correctly substituted in the case; and further that whether the petitioner party filed any objection against the inquiry report before the learned Magistrate concern and then upon elaborate discussion on the same and with a concurrent finding the learned Sessions Judge upheld the learned Magistrate state aforesaid judgment and order. But, our avenue is very narrow about to travel beyond our jurisdiction in re-examining those material evidences on record under section 561A of the code, in a case where the impugned judgment was passed under section 145, CrPC. Our Appellate Division in such situation in the case of Aminul Islam vs Mojibur Rahman, reported in 44 DLR (AD) 56, categorically held — 

 "The inherent jurisdiction of the High court Division will be available even to a party who has lost in revision before the Sessions Judge under section 561A. But it must be clearly borne in mind that the jurisdiction under section 561A is not to be used as an additional or an alternative jurisdiction. The powers hereunder being extra ordinary in nature should be exercised sparingly and with caution and only where such exercise is essential and justified by the tests specially laid down in the provision itself. It is now well-settled that a second revision does not lie to the High Court Division after 439A, CrPC vide Shafiqur Rahman vs NI Chowdhury, 35 DLR (AD) 127. The jurisdiction under section 561A cannot be invoked for the purpose of examining the correctness, legality or propriety of any finding, sentence or order recorded or passed by any inferior Criminal Court which is done in exercise of revisional jurisdiction under sections 435/439/439A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. A revision petition cannot be brought before the High Court Division in the camouflage of a petition under section 561A of the CrPC. The final order of a Magistrate passed under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which has been  upheld in revision, as in the present case, can  be interfered with under section 561A only to  prevent an abuse of the process of the Court  or otherwise to secure the ends of justice  which, in our opinion, is ordinarily relatable  to an exercise of authority without jurisdiction. It will be therefore, in a very rare case, that the High Court Division will feel called upon to exercise its jurisdiction under section 561A when the party has already exhausted the remedy of a revision. A proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be quashed under this section unless an abuse of the process of the court or an injustice appears apparently on the face of the record."
